Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
We're here to help! The information assembled here is for domestic students applying for admission to a graduate program at WMU.
Admission information
Learn more about graduate education at WMU by calling (269) 387-8212 or emailing @email.
Check out our virtual campus tour here.
Need help completing your online application? We're just a phone call or an email away! (269) 387-2228 or (269) 387-2025, @email.
Watch our video to guide you through your online application for admission here.
International Graduate Students
I'm an international applicant. Is there someone who can help me with my application, student visa, transcripts, and other questions?
For prospective international students and applicants, the WMU International Student and Scholar Services website includes information and a list of Frequently Asked Questions for prospective, admitted, and current international students. They can also be reached by email @email or phone (269) 387-5865.

Application Processing
I am submitting by the application deadline, but my recommenders have not yet submitted their responses and I just ordered my official transcripts so they're on the way. Is my application still considered on time?
Please contact your academic department to learn more about their specific guidelines. Some departments begin reviewing applications once all materials have been received, while others will consider your application on time as long as it was submitted before the deadline and supporting documents are still in transit. Reaching out to your department is the best way to understand their expectations.
How long should I wait for my application to be processed?
We ask that you please allow between 7 to 10 business days for processing applications and transcripts. Processing times may be longer, up to 14 business days, during peak times due to volume, including just before the start of a semester.
I entered my card information so why is my application is still showing 99% complete.
After you enter your credit card for payment, the last steps include:
Type your name for the electronic signature
Click the Verify box
Click the Submit box
Your application will show 100% complete and you will see your checklist indicating we have received your application.
When should I expect a decision?
Each department varies when they complete application reviews. Please contact your academic department for more information.
How do I know when a decision has been made on my application?
Your academic department will send your admission letter either by email or by mail. In addition, you will receive an email from WMU at the address listed on your application notifying you that a decision has been made and prompting you to log in to your WMU application portal to view it.
Bronco NetID and WIN
What is a Bronco NetID?
A Bronco NetID serves as your username for all things WMU related! You will use your Bronco NetID and email address for WMU student access-only services, such as registering for classes, reviewing financial aid information, accessing WMU email, and more.
What is a WIN?
A WIN is a student’s Western Identification Number (WIN). To obtain your WIN, log in to the application portal and click on View Your Decision. The WIN is listed in the top right corner of your university admission letter.
When do I get a Bronco NetID?
For domestic applicants, you will receive your Bronco NetID and temporary password three days after your admission to the University. Students will receive an email from the Office of Information Technology (WMU OIT Web Apps Admin Team). The email will contain your Bronco NetID and your WMU email address. If you need assistance, please contact the Help Desk (269) 387-4357.
If you are a current WMU undergraduate student who has been accepted into a graduate program, you will receive a “Connect to GoWMU” email encouraging you to log in to your GoWMU with your existing username and password.
I haven't received my login credentials from OIT.
If you haven’t received your login credentials by 5 p.m. within three days of being admitted, please check your spam or junk folder. If you still don’t see them, contact the Help Desk at (269) 387-4357 or helpdesk@wmich.edu.
Change of Program and Entry Term
How do I switch to a different program?
To switch to a different academic program, you'll need to submit a new degree-seeking application. If you're considering a program change within the same academic department, be sure to consult with your graduate advisor beforehand to discuss your options.
Can I change my entry term?
If you need to change your entry term, please contact your academic department. If they approve the request, they will notify the Graduate College to process the update. Non-degree and SCOPE students should contact @email to request a change term.
Funding and Financial Aid
What funding opportunities for graduate students exist at WMU?
Funding opportunities are offered primarily through the academic departments, but a few additional sites that could be helpful include:
WMU Graduate College Fellowships and Grants
WMU Graduate College External Funding Sources
Office of Research and Innovation External Funding Sources
WMU Handshake site for on-campus employment opportunities (WMU Bronco NetID and password required)
WMU Scholarship Universe
How do I know what graduate assistantships are available, such as a teaching assistant position?
Each department varies in their graduate assistantship opportunities. Please contact your academic department for information including application details and deadlines.
Who can I contact with questions regarding federal financial aid?
For any questions related to federal financial aid, please contact the Bronco Express service team. They can be reached by phone at 269-387-6000 or by email at finaid-info@wmich.edu. Walk-in assistance is also available at the Office of Student Financial Aid, located in the Faunce Student Services Building on main campus.
GRE Test Scores
GRE, TOEFL and Financial Aid Codes:
GRE- 1902
TOEFL- 1902
FAFSA- 002330
How do I schedule the GRE, and how do I send my scores to WMU?
WMU does not administer the GRE exam. To schedule your exam, please visit the GRE scheduling page at ets.org/gre.html, where you’ll find several testing options — including taking the exam online from home. Choose a format that works best for you!
The GRE website includes a section on preparing for the exam, so you'll want to check that out, too! You can take the exam anywhere and the results will be sent to the institutions you request (be sure to include WMU!). Western Michigan University’s school code is 1902.
My program requires the GRE. How do I submit the scores?
If your program requires the GRE, please request your official scores through ets.org. Western Michigan University’s school code is 1902.
Does WMU offer GRE or TOEFL test preparation?
The WMU Writing Center provides advice and test preparation for clients taking the Graduate Records Examination(GRE) and the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) exams. Information is available here.
I have additional questions about the GRE/GMAT. Who should I contact?
For any GRE or GMAT‑related questions, please contact your academic department. Some departments that require these exams/scores may allow you to request a waiver, so the department can provide the most accurate guidance.
Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
What is the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) requirement?
The Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) course is required to comply with requirements from national funding agencies and ensures that all graduate students at WMU are working to the highest possible standards of integrity.
All new master’s and doctoral graduate students must complete the RCR course. Graduate students are automatically enrolled in the course and will receive an introductory email, sent to their WMU email address. There is no fee for the course, and no credit hours are earned. This is a university-wide requirement and is not associated directly with any specific graduate program.
Click here for more information including how to access the RCR course, an overview, and course deadlines.
What happens if I don't complete the RCR requirement by the deadline?
A registration hold will be placed on the student account for those who do not complete the RCR course by the deadline, restricting them from registering for future classes. The hold will be lifted when the course is completed successfully. Need more info? Click here or contact the Course Facilitator at @email.
Recommendations
My recommender has not submitted anything yet. How do I send them a reminder through the application system?
Please log in to your graduate application portal and click on the appropriate application. The application checklist will be on the right. For each recommender, there are two options:
1) Change Recommender
2) Send Reminder
If you encounter difficulties, please contact us at @email.
Can I replace a recommender?
In most cases, yes, you can replace the recommender if they have not yet submitted a recommendation for you. Simply log in to your application portal here and click "Change Recommender" button to enter a new name and new email address.
Can I list more then 3?
Yes, however, doing so may delay the department’s review of your application. It’s important to regularly monitor your checklist. For any questions or concerns, please email admissions-graduate@wmich.edu.
Will the original recommender know that I swapped them out?
If you replace a recommender with someone else, when the original recommender clicks on the recommendation link, they will receive a message stating that it is no longer valid.
Who should I list as a recommender?
This varies by academic department. Here are some helpful tips and reminders:
This is an important decision because recommendations are an essential component used in combination with the other requirements by the review committee to inform an admission decision.
Program-specific requirements may be listed here if instructions from the department have been provided to the Graduate College. If not, we suggest that you carefully select recommenders who know you and are familiar with your work. They will be asked to complete a skill set rating sheet and upload an optional letter of recommendation on your behalf.
Contact your academic department for additional insight.
Can I send a recommender a request prior to clicking Submit on my application?
Yes, your recommender can submit their responses even before you have completed the application. Upon entering the recommender name and email address into the application system, they will immediately be emailed a link to the recommendation form even if applicants have not yet clicked Submit.
We do, however, first recommend that students complete all required fields for each recommender. Otherwise, the system will not allow applicants to submit the application or to revise/complete the recommender information after the recommender has submitted their responses.
My recommender could not open the email or complete the rating sheet, but they wrote a letter of recommendation. Is that ok?
That may be acceptable! Please email us at @email and we will contact your academic department to determine if they will accept the letter of recommendation without the rating sheet.
If the department responds confirming that they will accept the letter of recommendation only, we ask that your recommender email us with their letter of recommendation to @email, so we can manually attach it to your application.
If the department requires the rating sheet in addition to the letter of recommendation, we will email you to let you know and recommend that you either change recommender or obtain a new email address so you can send a new request to your recommender.
How will I know when a recommender submits the form?
When you log in to your application portal, you will see the required checklist items listed. A green checkmark indicates the item has been received and a red X indicates the item is outstanding. If any information is missing and you have questions, please email @email.
Transcripts
Do I need to submit a transcript if I graduated with my bachelor’s degree from WMU?
No, applicants who have attended or graduated from WMU do not need to request an official transcript from WMU.
Do I need to upload my transcripts into my application?
Yes, you should upload your unofficial transcripts when you submit your application. Doing so helps prevent processing delays, and some departments may consider reviewing your application while your official transcripts are still being processed. If you are still completing your bachelor’s degree, you should upload your current unofficial transcript; if admitted, you will then be required to submit an official transcript showing your conferred degree.
What official transcripts should I send? (For domestic applicants only)
Western Michigan University requires official transcripts sent directly from the issuing institution, through a third-party service, or credit evaluation company. An official transcript from the institution from which you received your bachelor degree is required, as well as a transcript from the institution(s) where any additional graduate level courses or degrees have been taken/completed. Some graduate programs may require an official transcripts from each institution attended after high school. It is best to check with the academic department, contact the Graduate College, or review the Additional Program Requirements website (learn more at wmich.edu/grad/program-allprograms).
Where do I have my transcripts sent? (For domestic applicants only)
Official transcripts must be sent directly from the issuing institution, through a third-party service, or credit evaluation company to be considered official. Please have official transcripts sent to one of the addresses below. If you are currently completing a degree, your transcript will show work in progress. If you are admitted to a graduate program, you will be required to send a final official transcript showing your degree and the date conferred.
Official transcripts may be sent in one of three ways:
Electronic: Official transcripts can be submitted electronically by the issuing institution through a credentialing service such as Parchment, DiplomaSender, Naviance, or National Clearinghouse. To be considered official, transcripts must be sent directly from the issuing institution, through a third-party service, or credit evaluation company to our office at @email. Once ordered, they typically take 5–10 business days to arrive and be processed (processing may take longer during peak periods). If your issuing institution does not allow you to select this email address, it is instead likely defaulting to the WMU Undergraduate Office of Admission address which is perfectly acceptable! We can still process your transcript if it is sent there.
Mail: Western Michigan University, Graduate College, 1903 W Michigan Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49008-5242 USA. Transcripts need to be enclosed in an official school envelope and include an authorized signature across the seal. Once ordered, they typically take 7–10 business days to arrive and be processed (processing may take longer during peak periods).
Hand-delivered: Obtain an official copy of your official transcript in a sealed envelope and bring it to the Graduate College admissions team in 120 W. Walwood Hall on east campus. Transcripts must be sealed in an official school envelope and include an authorized signature across the seal.
College transcripts must be received within 90 days of the print date on the transcript to be considered official. If you mail your materials, you may wish to have them sent through a mail service that provides delivery confirmation or a receipt showing that WMU received them (but this is not required).
What do I need to submit if my previous degree was earned outside the United States? (For domestic applicants with international transcripts only)
Students who earned a degree outside of the US must provide either a credit evaluation or your official transcripts translated into English. An official credit evaluation may be submitted in place of an official transcript directly from the issuing institution, third party service, or credit evaluation company. A credit evaluation, like those provided by ECE (ece.org) or WES (wes.org), typically includes all necessary information, such as your degree, graduation date, and coursework. The issuing institution/third party/credit evaluation company can send the evaluation directly to @email or the mailing address listed above.
I previously applied to WMU. Do you still have my transcripts on file?
If you have previously applied to WMU, we may already have your transcripts on file! Email us at @email so we can check on that for you. If we have your original transcript(s) on file, you will not need to request a new one unless you completed additional graduate work after we received your previous transcript.
What if I have transcripts from overseas?
All international transcripts must be translated into English by the issuing institution or a certified third-party translator. An official credit evaluation may be submitted in place of an official transcript.
Do I need to submit official transcripts from every institution I have attended?
Most graduate programs require only the official transcript from the institution where applicants earned their bachelor's degree and where any graduate coursework was completed.
However, a handful of WMU programs require official transcripts from every institution attended after high school. This varies by department and program so please click here to review the specific requirements for the program to which you are applying. Some programs with additional requirements for transcripts include:
Counselor Education certificate, master’s, and doctoral programs (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school)
History master's program (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school)
Marriage, Couple, and Family Counseling master's program (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school)
Occupational Therapy (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school to OTCAS application only; the WMU application for admission requires official transcripts from the bachelor's degree-granting institution as well as any institution where graduate credits were earned)
Physician Assistant (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school to CASPA application only; the WMU application for admission requires official transcripts from the bachelor's degree-granting institution as well as any institution where graduate credits were earned)
Physical Therapy (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school to PTCAS application only; the WMU application for admission requires official transcripts from the bachelor's degree-granting institution as well as any institution where graduate credits were earned)
School Counseling master's, graduate certificate program (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school)
Speech Pathology (submit official transcripts from every institution attended after high school to CSDCAS application only; the WMU application for admission requires official transcripts from the bachelor's degree-granting institution as well as any institution where graduate credits were earned)
Do I need to submit a transcript with my graduate program application if I am still working on my bachelor’s degree at my current school?
Yes, official transcripts are required to complete your application, even if it shows work in progress. If you are admitted to the program, you will have your issuing institution send a final transcript, showing your degree and the date conferred.
Newly Admitted Students
Congratulations on your admission! The department that admitted you will be in touch soon with details about your next steps. In the meantime, if you have any questions, feel free to contact your graduate advisor.
Within three days of your admission, you should received an email from OIT to your personal email address on file. This email will contain your Bronco NetID and WMU email information. Once you have your Bronco NetID and password, you may log into goWMU. If you do not receive your Bronco NetID email, please contact the WMU Help Desk at (269) 387-4357 or @email for assistance.
If you're admitted as a Graduate: Non-Degree seeking or SCOPE student, you will receive an email from the Graduate Admissions Office regarding next steps.
Non-Degree Graduate
What is Non-Degree Graduate, and how do I know if it is right for me?
If you have a bachelor’s degree and are not planning to pursue a degree or graduate certificate program, you can apply for non-degree seeking status to take classes (undergraduate or graduate). Non-Degree status may limit both your course selection and is not eligible for federal financial aid. Contact the department in which you wish to take a course regarding any course restrictions for non-degree students. Please note that acceptance for non-degree does not constitute admission to a WMU graduate program.
How do I apply for Non-Degree Graduate? (Domestic applicants only)
To start your Non-Degree Graduate application, you will need to visit the Graduate application portal: wmich.edu/grad/apply. Please make sure you are using Chrome or Firefox browsers for the best compatibility.
Instructions:
Once you have logged into the WMU Graduate Application Portal, please follow these steps:
1. Click the blue “Start New” button on the right-hand side.
2. Select the brown “Start Application” button located under Graduate Degree, Graduate Non-Degree and Scope-Graduate.
3. To populate the correct application, select the following options:
o Status: Domestic
o Degree Option: Non-Degree – Graduate
o Campus: Main Campus (Kalamazoo) (*even if you plan to take online courses)
o Program: Non-Degree – Graduate
o Re-applying: No
o Term: Select your preferred entry term. (fall, spring, summer 1, or summer 2)
4. Click the brown “Start Application” button to get started. Please fill out the application, pay the application fee, electronically provide your signature, and submit your application completely.
What are the application requirements?
The only application requirement for Non-Degree Graduate is proof of your undergraduate degree, like an unofficial transcript or a picture of your diploma. You will upload this document in your application and it should show the name of the issuing institution, your name, the degree and the date conferred.
If the application asks for recommendations, please list N/A for the name and @email. It is a data error glitch and will not be used for processing your application.
How long does the application take to be processed?
Applications are typically processed the day after submission. Sometimes during peak processing times there may be extended time frames for processing Non-Degree Graduate applications. Check for any updates by logging into your account to see the dashboard. You can also contact the Graduate College at @email who can provide an update on the application.
Where can I view the course(s) and the seat availability?
You can visit wmich.edu/classlookup to view available courses and the seat availability. A Bronco NetID and password are not required to use the new class search tool. If you need assistance on navigating the new tool, please see the instructional notes at wmich.edu/registrar/courses. You can also contact the Office of Registrar at (269) 387-4300 or @email for further assistance. If you wish to enroll in a restricted course, you will need to contact the department that offers the course for further guidance.
